os_type.title: ### `os_type` scalar value

0 = Windows

1 = macOS (pre v7.70)

2 = Linux (pre v7.70)

On v7.71+, 0 is returned for all platforms unless the theme specifies `want_os_type 1` in rtconfig.txt. In that case, macOS = 3 and Linux = 4.

v7.70 always reports 3 for macOS and 4 for Linux.

clear.title: ### `clear` command
clear.info: Clears a particular attribute (or wildcard list of attributes) to empty.

reset.title: ### `reset` command
reset.info: Resets a particular attribute (or wildcard list of attributes) to their default settings.

set.title: ### `set` command
set.info:
Sets an attribute or user variable to an expression.

Note that you do not need to declare user variables, simply setting them is sufficient. As a matter of etiquette, do not use `.` in user variables (although you can), names with `.` in them are reserved for future expansion.

def.title: ### `def` command
def.info: Defines a value to be replaced with another value (e.g. a preprocessor #define).
def.example:
def square10 10 10
set tcp.mute [0 0 square10] ; sets tcp.mute to [0 0 10 10]
def two_coords [10 10 0 0] [0 0 10 10]
set tcp.mute + two_coords   ; sets tcp.mute to [10 10 10 10]
set tcp.mute w<100 two_coords ; like set.tcp.mute w<100 [10 10 0 0] [0 0 10 10]

front.title: ### `front` command
front.info: Brings an element to the front of the Z order. Note that the ordering of elements is static and can't be affected by logic.

macro.title: ### `macro` command
macro.info:
Defines a macro with any number of parameters which can be used later.

Note that using `##` in a macro allows the parameter to be concatenated with another named string.
macro.example:
macro setall dest src
  set dest [src src src src src src src src]
  set master.##dest dest
endmacro
setall tcp.mute 1  ; set tcp.mute [1 1 1 1 1 1 1], set master.tcp.mute tcp.mute

define_parameter.title: ### `define_parameter` command
define_parameter.info:
Defines a ReaScript-accessible user-defined parameter which the WALTER code can use.

The default theme adjuster script will allow tweaking the first 10 parameters. Note that variable name is used to make the value persist for this theme
define_parameter.example:
;                variable name     description for user   default  minimum maximum
define_parameter "hide_mute"       "Hide Mute Button"     0        0       1
; later in script
set tcp.mute hide_mute==1 [0] ; hide tcp.mute if hide_mute is set

custom.title: ### `custom` command
custom.info:
Defines a custom element.

Note that the custom element name must include the string `custom`. Custom elements become a normal part of the layout that contains them and can be used with `set`, `front`, etc. If `command_id` is specified and valid, and `button_image` is a valid image name, element will be a button. Otherwise, it will be a static text element with `text_label`. `tcp.custom.xyz.font`, `.color` and `.margin` may all be specified.

layout.title: ### `layout` command
layout.info:
Theme author can define layouts, by using the commands `layout` and `lndLayout`.

When defining a layout, it inherits the behavior from the parent (or default) layout (at the time of first use in that UI context).

The `layout` command can take one or two paraemeters - the first parameter defines the name of that layout, and the optional second parameter defines the theme image subdirectory to use for that layout.

You can specify multiple layouts with the same name, and they will be treated similar to a single layout definiton, though for clarity it might be good to separate them based on the UI context (i.e. tcp.*, mcp.*, etc). If you define layouts with the same name for various UI contexts, you may wish to expose them as a global theme layout using `globalLayout`, which then lists that layout in the main layout list.
layout.example:
layout "Mute button mixer"
  clear mcp.*
  set mcp.size [20 20]
  set mcp.mute [0 0 20 20 0 0 1 1]
endLayout

An empty `requested_layout_name` can be used to match the default layout.
